notable_absence.finding: Same as BEGIN TRANSACTION and ROLLBACK TRANSACTION: SAVEPOINT carries no access-control gate at all. Its only stated prerequisite is behavioral ('You may only use this statement within a transaction') and its only other rule is a naming-collision behavior ('If a savepoint with the same name already exists, the existing savepoint is replaced.'). The transaction-statement family is uniformly ungated across all four members examined so far (BEGIN/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT), strengthening the hypothesis that this is a deliberate, consistent design choice rather than a per-page omission.

cross_component_finding: Same shared-source-content pattern as begin-transaction.json and rollback-transaction.json: links to server/'s transaction overview ('For an overview of Couchbase transactions, see [Transactions](../../../server/current/learn/data/transactions.md)') and the same Couchbase blog post, rather than any Capella-specific content.
cross_product_finding: Per the cross-round transaction check: no textual evidence on this page connects SAVEPOINT to the Java SDK's distributed-transaction feature (sdk:distributed-transaction). Related Links are exclusively to other SQL++ transaction statements, the server/ overview, and the Couchbase blog post. No SDK cross-reference is present, so no relation is asserted; open question remains open, consistent with begin-transaction.json and rollback-transaction.json in this same round.
